task.description: Fix the reason-truncation to match Postgres's actual codepoint-based length semantics, not grapheme-based. Recommended approach: truncate by codepoint count (e.g. `error_args.reason |> String.codepoints() |> Enum.take(255) |> Enum.join()`), since Ecto's own validate_length/3 also counts graphemes by default and would not catch this either -- codepoint-based truncation is the precise match for Postgres's varchar(n) semantics. Apply this fix at lib/letflow/engine/execution_error.ex:229 (and check whether the equivalent risk exists anywhere else this run introduced a truncated string into a bounded column, e.g. Hook A's dlq_attrs building in engine.ex -- audit for the same pattern). Add a regression test using a combining-mark string (e.g. 300 repetitions of a base character plus a combining diacritic) that would have exceeded the column limit under the old grapheme-based truncation, asserting the DLQ insert succeeds and the reason column's actual byte/codepoint length is within bounds. Run mix format on touched files, then mix compile --warnings-as-errors and mix test yourself and quote real output.
acceptance_criteria: reason truncation is codepoint-count-based, not grapheme-count-based, guaranteeing the result never exceeds the dlq_entries.reason column's actual Postgres varchar(255) limit regardless of combining-mark content
